subproblem.title: A product measure whose transversal measure is carried by a countable set is a countable sum of weighted parallel planes
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace, σ a Borel measure on ℝ^P, and Z ⊆ ℝ^P a countable set with σ(ℝ^P∖Z) = 0. Let ν be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then ν = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V}. That is, ν is the Measure.sum, over the subtype Z, of the measures σ({w})•(Hⁿ restricted to {y : y − w ∈ V}).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν σ : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (Z : Set (Euclid P)), Z.Countable → σ Zᶜ = 0 → (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → ν A = ∫⁻ t in (V : Set (Euclid P)), σ ((fun y => t + y) ⁻¹' A) ∂μHE[n]) → ν = Measure.sum (fun w : Z => σ {(w : Euclid P)} • (μHE[n]).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - w ∈ V})
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 ("σ is a sum of point masses") and 6 ("ν is a sum of planes") of the parent proof. In the parent, Z = {w ∈ V^⊥ : ofReal c ≤ σ({w})} is countable with σ(ℝ^P∖Z) = 0 by steps 3–4. Neither the dimension of V nor Z ⊆ V^⊥ is used here.
Notation: (D) is the hypothesis ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for Borel A. Sums Σ_{w∈Z} are unconditional sums (tsum) in [0, ∞] over the subtype Z, which is a countable type because Z is a countable set (Set.Countable.to_subtype). 1_S is the indicator function of S, with values in {0, 1} ⊆ [0, ∞].
1. (σ is a sum of point masses.) Let S ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel. Since σ(ℝ^P∖Z) = 0, σ(S) = σ(S ∩ Z) (measure_inter_conull). Moreover S ∩ Z = ⋃_{w∈Z}(S ∩ {w}): a point y ∈ S ∩ Z lies in the term with w = y, and every term is contained in S ∩ Z. The sets S ∩ {w} (w ∈ Z) are Borel, since singletons are closed. They are pairwise disjoint, since for w ≠ w′ the singletons {w} and {w′} are disjoint. The index type Z is countable, so countable additivity (measure_iUnion) gives σ(S ∩ Z) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ(S ∩ {w}). For each w ∈ Z: if w ∈ S then S ∩ {w} = {w}, so σ(S ∩ {w}) = σ({w}) = σ({w})·1_S(w); if w ∉ S then S ∩ {w} = ∅, so σ(S ∩ {w}) = 0 = σ({w})·1_S(w). Hence σ(S) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·1_S(w) for every Borel S.
2. (Insertion into (D).) Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and t ∈ ℝ^P. The set S_t := {y : t + y ∈ A} is Borel, being the preimage of A under the continuous map y ↦ t + y, and 1_{S_t}(w) = 1_A(t + w) for every w. By step 1, σ(S_t) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·1_A(t + w). Therefore (D) gives ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·1_A(t + w) dHⁿ(t).
3. (Exchange of sum and integral.) For each w ∈ Z, the function t ↦ 1_A(t + w) is Borel measurable (A is Borel and t ↦ t + w is continuous), hence so is t ↦ σ({w})·1_A(t + w). Since the index type Z is countable, the monotone convergence theorem for series of nonnegative measurable functions (lintegral_tsum) and pulling out the constant (lintegral_const_mul) give ν(A) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·∫⁻_{t∈V}1_A(t + w) dHⁿ(t).
4. (Translation.) Fix w ∈ Z and put A − w := {t : t + w ∈ A}, a Borel set with 1_A(t + w) = 1_{A−w}(t). Then ∫⁻_{t∈V}1_{A−w}(t) dHⁿ(t) = (Hⁿ⌞V)(A − w) = Hⁿ((A − w) ∩ V) (lintegral_indicator_one, Measure.restrict_apply). The translation τ(t) := t + w is an isometry of ℝ^P (isometry_add_right). Hⁿ = μHE[n] is invariant under isometries: Hⁿ(τ(S)) = Hⁿ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^P (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). Moreover τ((A − w) ∩ V) = A ∩ {y : y − w ∈ V}. Indeed, if t + w ∈ A and t ∈ V, then y := τ(t) = t + w ∈ A and y − w = t ∈ V. Conversely, if y ∈ A and y − w ∈ V, then t := y − w satisfies t + w = y ∈ A, t ∈ V and τ(t) = y. Hence ∫⁻_{t∈V}1_A(t + w) dHⁿ(t) = Hⁿ(A ∩ {y : y − w ∈ V}) = (Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A) (Measure.restrict_apply; A is Borel).
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 3 and 4, ν(A) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·(Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A). This equals Σ_{w∈Z}(σ({w})•Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A) (Measure.smul_apply), which equals (Measure.sum_{w∈Z}σ({w})•Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A) because A is Borel (Measure.sum_apply). This holds for every Borel A, so the two measures are equal (Measure.ext). ∎
proof_key_steps: For Borel S, σ(S) = σ(S ∩ Z) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ(S ∩ {w}) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·1_S(w), by countable additivity over the countable set Z.
Inserting this with S = {y : t + y ∈ A} into the product formula and exchanging sum and integral (lintegral_tsum) gives ν(A) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·Hⁿ(V ∩ {t : t + w ∈ A}).
Translation by w is an isometry carrying V ∩ {t : t + w ∈ A} onto A ∩ {y : y − w ∈ V}, and Hⁿ is isometry invariant, so ν(A) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·(Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A).
Measure.sum_apply and Measure.ext give the identity of measures.

audit.reason: Countable additivity over disjoint singletons establishes the atomic expansion. The measurable nonnegative summands justify exchanging sum and integral without σ-finiteness. Translation isometry identifies each restricted plane measure, and Measure.sum_apply plus extensionality proves the exact identity. Neither dim V = n nor Z ⊆ Vᗮ is needed.
